mainTopic: Who is obligated in סוכה (women, גרים, minors), and living in the סוכה as one's permanent home.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a challenge from the previous amud. Why do we need a special הלכה to exempt women from סוכה, and a verse to include women in יום הכפורים, when general rules already seem to cover both? אביי and רבא each explain why the הלכה for סוכה was still needed. The גמרא then shows that the verse 'האזרח' includes גרים in סוכה, and that the יום הכפורים verse obligates women in תוספת עינוי. Next it explains that 'כל' includes only a minor who has reached חינוך, and that this is מדרבנן with the verse as an אסמכתא. It defines a child who 'no longer needs his mother', and explains the story of שמאי הזקן making a סוכה for a newborn as following שמאי's stricter view. A new משנה teaches that the סוכה is one's permanent home for seven days, that heavy rain lets one leave, and gives a parable explaining what rain means. The גמרא ends by teaching from תשבו כעין תדורו how to live in the סוכה, including that review of Torah happens there while deep analysis is done outside.

steps.title: The Torah equates women to men for all punishments
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the challenge. Women are already included in יום הכפורים through the principle that the Torah equates women to men for every punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse made a woman equal to a man for all the punishments in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of רב יהודה אמר רב, which it used as part of its challenge. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכפורים has איסורים and the punishment of כרת. Under this principle, women are automatically obligated like men. So a separate verse to include women in יום הכפורים seems unnecessary, just as a הלכה to exempt women from סוכה seemed unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishments (and the prohibitions that carry them)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new teaching. It is the tail end of a quote, brought as part of a challenge that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: The verse equated a woman to a man
phrases.notes: End of the teaching of רב יהודה אמר רב

phrases.english: for all punishments in the Torah.
phrases.notes: So women are obligated in יום הכפורים automatically

steps.triggerLanguage: הִשְׁוָה הַכָּתוּב אִשָּׁה לְאִישׁ לְכׇל עוֹנָשִׁין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for separate sources: a הלכה exempting women from סוכה, and a verse including women in יום הכפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both results already follow from general rules: women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות, and women equal men for all punishments. So the extra sources seem redundant.

steps.title: אביי: the הלכה was needed because סוכה is like normal dwelling
steps.stepSummary: אביי says סוכה really is a הלכה, and it was needed. Without it, we might think that 'תשבו' means 'live as you normally live,' and a husband and wife normally live together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, the women's exemption from סוכה is a הלכה, and it was needed. You might have thought that 'you shall sit' means 'like you live at home.' Just as a home is lived in by a man and his wife, so too a סוכה would be for a man and his wife. So the הלכה teaches us that women are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge about סוכה. He explains why women's exemption needed its own source even though it is a time-bound מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule exempts women from time-bound מצוות. But סוכה follows the principle of תשבו כעין תדורו, that you live in it the way you live in your house. Since a normal home includes the wife, we might have made an exception and obligated women. The הלכה blocks that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: A הלכה למשה מסיני, a tradition received orally
It might have entered your mind to say
'Sit' in the סוכה the way you normally dwell

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of תשבו כעין תדורו is a basic principle in the laws of סוכה. It shapes how one eats, sleeps and lives in the סוכה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Actually, sukkah is a halacha, and it was necessary.
phrases.notes: Even though it is a time-bound מצוה

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say
'You shall sit' means like you dwell,
just as dwelling is a man and his wife,
so too sukkah is a man and his wife,
it teaches us (that women are exempt).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם סוּכָּה הִלְכְתָא, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the סוכה half of the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the source is not redundant, because there was a reason to think the general rule would not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a סוכה must be lived in like a home, and a home includes one's wife, women would be obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה teaches that women are exempt from סוכה.

steps.title: רבא: the הלכה was needed to block a comparison to פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different reason the הלכה was needed. We might have compared סוכות to פסח through a גזירה שוה on the words 'fifteenth'. Women are obligated in מצה, so they would also be obligated in סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It was needed. You might have thought to learn 'fifteenth' (said about סוכות) from 'fifteenth' (said about the חג המצות). Just as there women are obligated, so too here women are obligated. So the הלכה teaches us that women are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers another answer to the same question. The danger he points to is a גזירה שוה with פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both festivals are described as falling on the 'fifteenth' of the month. Women are obligated to eat מצה even though it is time-bound, so a גזירה שוה would have carried that obligation over to סוכה. The הלכה tells us not to make this comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Fifteenth (the shared word for the גזירה שוה)
Just as there, so too here

steps.confusionAlert: Women's obligation in מצה is itself an exception to the time-bound rule. It is learned from the link between eating מצה and the איסור of חמץ. That exception is exactly why the comparison was a real risk.

phrases.english: Rava said: It was necessary,
it might enter your mind to say
derive 'fifteenth' and 'fifteenth'
from the festival of matzos.
Just as there, women are obligated,
so too here, women are obligated.
It teaches us (that they are exempt).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same challenge that אביי answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the source is not redundant, because it blocks a possible גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Through the גזירה שוה of 'fifteenth' with פסח, women would be obligated in סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה teaches that women are exempt from סוכה.

steps.title: If the exemption is a הלכה, what does the verse add?
steps.stepSummary: If women's exemption from סוכה comes from a הלכה, then the verse 'האזרח' seems to have no job.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said סוכה is a הלכה, why do I need the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the purpose of the verse. It sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally, 'האזרח' seemed to be the source for exempting women. Once the exemption comes from a הלכה, the verse's wording looks extra, and the גמרא demands to know what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that you have said
Why do I need the verse?

phrases.english: And now that you said sukkah is a halacha,
why do I need the verse?
phrases.notes: Referring to 'האזרח' in the סוכה verse

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ סוּכָּה הִלְכְתָא, קָרָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that the exemption is a הלכה, then questions the verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The verse 'האזרח' in the סוכה passage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the הלכה already exempts women, the verse seems to have nothing left to teach.

steps.title: The verse comes to include converts
steps.stepSummary: The verse teaches that גרים are obligated in סוכה. Otherwise 'האזרח בישראל' (the native-born) might have suggested they are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include converts. You might have thought: the Torah said 'the native-born in Israel' and not converts. So it teaches us that converts are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the verse a new job: including גרים in the מצוה of סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word 'אזרח' could sound like it means only born Jews. The added wording of the verse shows that גרים are included. So the verse is no longer extra.

phrases.english: To include the converts.
It might enter your mind to say:
'The homeborn in Israel' said the Merciful One,
and not the converts,
it teaches us (that converts are obligated).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the verse a new purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: Women are exempt from סוכה through a הלכה. The verse 'האזרח' is used to include גרים.

steps.title: יום הכפורים is already covered by רב יהודה's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the יום הכפורים verse. Women's obligation there already comes from רב יהודה אמר רב, so what does 'האזרח' add?
steps.simpleTranslation: יום הכפורים is derived from what רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the יום הכפורים verse and points out that it seems redundant. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since women equal men for all punishments, women automatically fast on יום הכפורים. So the verse including women there seems to have no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: יום הכפורים, the Day of Atonement
It is derived / it comes out from

phrases.english: Yom Kippur
is derived from what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the יום הכפורים half of the original challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Women are already included through the principle that women equal men for all punishments.

steps.title: The verse obligates women in the added time of fasting
steps.stepSummary: The verse is needed for תוספת עינוי, the extra time added to the fast. That period carries no עונש and no אזהרה, so the general rule would not have obligated women.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed only for the added time of affliction. You might have thought: since the Torah removed the added time from punishment and from the warning-prohibition, women are not obligated in it at all. So it teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the יום הכפורים verse obligates women in the extra time added before and after the fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's rule only covers מצוות that carry punishments and prohibitions. תוספת עינוי has neither, so women would not be included through that rule. The verse teaches that women must observe the added time as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Adding to the fast (extra time before and after יום הכפורים)

steps.whatToRemember: Women are exempt from סוכה through a הלכה, and the verse includes גרים. Women fast on יום הכפורים through רב יהודה אמר רב, and the verse adds that they keep תוספת עינוי as well.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that women are obligated in תוספת יום הכפורים, even though that period carries no כרת and no לאו.

phrases.english: It was needed only for the extension of affliction.
It might enter your mind to say:
since the Merciful One excluded the extension of affliction
from punishment and from prohibition,
women are not obligated at all,
it teaches us (that they are obligated).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the verse to a case the general rule does not cover.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since תוספת עינוי has no punishment or prohibition, רב יהודה's rule would not include women.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women are obligated in תוספת עינוי.

steps.title: Minors included by 'all' versus the משנה that exempts minors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that 'כל' includes minors, then challenges it from the משנה that says minors are exempt from סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: the word 'all' comes to include minors. But we learned in the משנה: women, slaves, and minors are exempt from סוכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the ברייתא it quoted earlier and asks how it fits with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא read the extra word 'כל' in 'כל האזרח' as adding minors to the obligation. Our משנה states plainly that minors are exempt. The two sources seem to say opposite things.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', the formula for quoting back an earlier source in order to discuss it
To include, to add something through an extra word
Minors, children under בר מצוה age
'But we learned in a משנה', which introduces a contradiction

phrases.english: The Master said: 'All' comes to include the minors.
But we learned: women, slaves, and minors
are exempt from the sukka!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's derivation, after the discussion in steps 1 to 7 (women, then גרים and תוספת עינוי), to look at its claim about minors.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that 'כל' includes minors
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly exempts minors, so a verse cannot be including them.

steps.title: Two kinds of minors
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a minor who has reached חינוך. The משנה is talking about a minor who has not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it means a minor who has reached the age of training. There, it means a minor who has not reached the age of training.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different age of child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child old enough to be trained in מצוות is the one 'included'. A child too young for training is the one the משנה exempts. Both sources stay correct.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
Here… there; each source refers to a different case
Training a child to do מצוות

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
Here, with a minor who reached the age of training;
there, with a minor who did not reach the age of training.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources refer to the same kind of minor and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to a minor at the age of חינוך. The משנה refers to a younger minor.

steps.title: But חינוך is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a minor's obligation through חינוך is מדרבנן, so a Torah verse should not be teaching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a minor who has reached the age of training is only obligated by rabbinic law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse 'כל' teaches about a minor at the age of חינוך, it sounds like a Torah-level law. Yet everyone knows חינוך is only a rabbinic obligation. So how can a verse be its source?

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not from the Torah itself

phrases.english: A minor who reached the age of training
is obligated only by rabbinic law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using a Torah verse to include a minor at the age of חינוך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic obligation cannot come from a Torah verse.

steps.title: The verse is just a hint
steps.stepSummary: Yes, the obligation is rabbinic. The verse is only an אסמכתא, a textual hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed rabbinic, and the verse is merely a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that חינוך is rabbinic. It explains that the verse is not the real source, only a hint the חכמים attached to their rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a verse the חכמים 'lean' their rabbinic law on. It does not create a Torah obligation. So the ברייתא's derivation does not clash with the fact that חינוך is מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A mere support: a verse used as a hint for a rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: A minor who has reached חינוך sits in the סוכה מדרבנן. The 'כל' in the verse is only an אסמכתא for that rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the minor becomes obligated from the Torah because a verse is cited. An אסמכתא never creates a Torah law.

phrases.english: It is indeed by rabbinic law,
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 10 and closes the discussion of minors in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the derivation as an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse makes a Torah-level obligation for the minor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The obligation is rabbinic, and the verse only hints at it.

steps.title: What is a minor who doesn't need his mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks how to define 'a minor who does not need his mother'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A minor who does not need his mother' is obligated. What is the case of a minor who does not need his mother?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for a clear definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה obligates such a child in סוכה but never says at what point a child stops 'needing his mother'. The גמרא wants a practical test.

keyTerms.meaning: Who does not need his mother
What is the case? How is it defined?

phrases.english: 'A minor who does not need his mother, etc.'

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי קָטָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְאִמּוֹ?
phrases.english: What are the circumstances of a minor who does not need his mother?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical definition of a child who no longer needs his mother.

steps.title: Definition of רבי ינאי's school: using the bathroom alone
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי says it is a child who relieves himself and does not need his mother to clean him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: any child who relieves himself and his mother does not wipe him.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer gives a test based on the child's independence in the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child who can take care of himself after using the bathroom is independent enough. Such a child is obligated in סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The study house (school) of רבי ינאי

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
Any child who relieves himself and his mother does not wipe him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Independence in the bathroom is the test.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's definition: waking without calling for Mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says it is a child who wakes up and does not call 'Mother, mother!'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: any child who wakes from his sleep and does not call 'Mother, mother!'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives a different test, based on how the child acts when he wakes up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here independence is emotional: the child does not need his mother the moment he wakes. This is an alternative to the bathroom test.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Any child who wakes from his sleep
and does not call 'Mother, mother!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not calling for his mother on waking is the test.

steps.title: Even older children call for Mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that even bigger children call their mother when they wake up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But older children also call out for their mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's test, because it would label even older, independent children as still needing their mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If calling 'Mother!' showed dependence, then even clearly independent older children would fail the test. So the test as stated cannot be right.

phrases.english: Older children also call out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's definition in step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Older, independent children also call their mother, so the test does not tell the two apart.

steps.title: It means calling over and over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the test: it is a child who does not keep calling 'Mother, mother!' repeatedly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: any child who wakes and does not call 'Mother, mother!' (again and again).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבי שמעון's test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An older child may call once, but if no one comes he manages alone. A young, dependent child keeps crying 'Mother, mother!' until she comes. The repeated calling is the sign of dependence.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: reread the statement this way

phrases.english: Rather, say: any child who wakes
and does not call 'Mother, mother!' (repeatedly).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any call for Mother shows dependence.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only nonstop, repeated calling shows dependence.

steps.title: Why tell a story that contradicts the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells how שמאי הזקן made a סוכה for his newborn grandson. The גמרא asks why a story that contradicts the rule is cited.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'It happened that his daughter-in-law gave birth…' Is a story brought to contradict the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה brings a story that seems to oppose what it just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said only a child who doesn't need his mother is obligated. Then it tells of שמאי making a סוכה even for a newborn. A story is normally brought to support a rule, not to undercut it.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story told as a precedent

phrases.english: 'It happened that his daughter-in-law gave birth, etc.'
Is an incident brought to contradict?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה is built: a story placed after a rule it seems to oppose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story should support the rule before it, yet this one goes against it.

steps.title: Missing words: שמאי is stricter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is missing a line. It should read that שמאי is strict, and the story illustrates his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: And שמאי is strict. And there was also an incident: the daughter-in-law of שמאי הזקן gave birth, and he broke away the plaster of the roof and covered the bed with סכך for the baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה left out a line saying שמאי disagrees. The story supports שמאי's view, not the majority rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words filled in, the story no longer contradicts anything. It proves that שמאי obligates even a newborn in סוכה. שמאי removed the plaster so the beams above the bed could serve as סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing something and must be filled in
And this is what it teaches
The plaster layer on top of the roof beams

steps.whatToRemember: The majority obligates only a child who no longer needs his mother, and even that only מדרבנן. שמאי is stricter, even for a newborn, and the story illustrates his view.

phrases.english: It is incomplete, and this is what it teaches:
And Shammai is stringent;
and there was also an incident where the daughter-in-law
of Shammai the Elder gave birth,
and he broke away the roof plaster
and roofed over the bed for the sake of the baby.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: filling in a missing line of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story contradicts the rule of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story supports שמאי's stricter view, which the full משנה states.

steps.title: New משנה: the סוכה is your main home
steps.stepSummary: For all seven days a person treats his סוכה as his permanent home and his house as temporary.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All seven days, a person makes his סוכה permanent and his house temporary.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, setting the basic rule for how one lives in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוכה is not only for a quick visit. For the whole holiday it becomes the person's main dwelling, the place where he eats, sleeps and spends time, while his house becomes secondary.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle (סוכה קבע, בית עראי) is the basis for many practical laws about which activities belong in the סוכה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All seven days

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה סוּכָּתוֹ קֶבַע, וּבֵיתוֹ עֲרַאי.
phrases.english: a person makes his sukka permanent and his house temporary.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה סוּכָּתוֹ קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During סוכות the סוכה is one's permanent home and the house is temporary.

steps.title: When rain lets you leave the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: If rain falls, one may leave once it is heavy enough to spoil a thick cooked dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: If rain fell, from when may one leave? From when the thick porridge would spoil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the measure of rain that frees a person from staying in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every drop is enough to leave. The test is rain strong enough to ruin a מקפה, a thick dish. At that point the סוכה is no longer a livable home.

keyTerms.meaning: To vacate, to leave the סוכה
A thick cooked dish, like porridge

phrases.english: If rain fell,
from when is it permitted to vacate?
From when the congealed dish would spoil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a limit to the rule of step 19: when the 'permanent home' may be left.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain heavy enough to spoil a מקפה permits leaving the סוכה.

steps.title: The parable of the servant and the jug
steps.stepSummary: Rain on סוכות is like a master who throws a jug of water in the face of his servant: a sign he is not wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told a parable: what is this like? A servant who came to pour a cup for his master, and the master poured a jug of water in his face.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a parable explaining what rain during סוכות means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servant wants to serve, but the master rejects his service in a pointed way. In the same way, rain forcing a person out of the סוכה is a sign that הקב״ה is not accepting his מצוה right now. It is a bad sign, not a convenience.

keyTerms.meaning: To pour or mix a cup of wine

steps.confusionAlert: In the parable it is the master who throws the water at the servant. The servant (the Jew) is the one being rejected.

phrases.english: They told a parable: to what is this matter comparable?
To a servant who came to pour a cup for his master,
and he poured a jug of water on his face.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning behind the rain rule of step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain on סוכות is a sign of divine displeasure, like a master rejecting his servant's service.

steps.title: Making the סוכה your real home
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains how a person makes his סוכה permanent and his house temporary.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The חכמים taught: For all seven days a person makes his סוכה his permanent home and his house temporary. How? If he has beautiful dishes, he brings them up to the סוכה. If he has beautiful bedding, he brings it up to the סוכה. He eats, drinks and relaxes in the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that gives practical examples of the משנה's rule from Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'סוכה is permanent, house is temporary.' The ברייתא shows what that looks like in real life: move your nicest things into the סוכה and do your normal daily living there.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
All seven days
a person makes his sukkah permanent
and his house temporary.
How so?
If he had beautiful vessels,
he brings them up to the sukkah;
phrases.notes: 'Up' because the sukkah was usually built on the roof.

phrases.english: beautiful bedding — he brings it up to the sukkah;
he eats, drinks and relaxes in the sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה סוּכָּתוֹ קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה line from Step 19 and fills in practical details.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Treating the סוכה as permanent means moving your nice dishes and bedding there and doing your eating, drinking and relaxing there.

steps.title: What is the source for this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the Torah this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the rule. This is a setup line for the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The גמרא simply wants to know which פסוק teaches that the סוכה must be lived in like a real home.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (derived)? A request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule just taught in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the סוכה must be treated as a permanent home.

steps.title: Live in it the way you live at home
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא derives the rule from the word תשבו, meaning 'live as you normally live,' and adds that one learns Torah in the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: 'You shall dwell' (תשבו) means 'the way you live at home.' From here they said: for all seven days a person makes his סוכה permanent and his house temporary. How? Beautiful dishes and bedding go up to the סוכה; he eats, drinks, relaxes and learns Torah in the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: the Torah's word תשבו tells us to live in the סוכה just like we live in our homes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah said 'dwell,' the סוכה must hold your whole normal life, not just a quick visit. This version of the ברייתא adds one new item: you also learn Torah in the סוכה. That new detail is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the way you live (in your home)

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: 'You shall dwell' —
like the way you live at home.
From here they said:
All seven days
a person makes his sukkah permanent
and his house temporary.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיצַד? הָיוּ לוֹ כֵּלִים נָאִים — מַעֲלָן לַסּוּכָּה,
phrases.english: How so? If he had beautiful vessels — he brings them up to the sukkah;
beautiful bedding — he brings it up to the sukkah;
he eats, drinks and relaxes in the sukkah
and studies Torah in the sukkah.
phrases.notes: This is the added detail not found in the first ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23 by giving the פסוק and its interpretation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word תשבו means 'live as you normally live,' so the סוכה becomes your permanent home, including for Torah study.
steps.whyThisMatters: תשבו כעין תדורו is the basic principle behind many הלכות of סוכה: whatever you normally do at home, you do in the סוכה.

steps.title: But רבא says deep study belongs outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges 'learning in the סוכה' from רבא, who says analysis of the משנה is done outside the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבא said: reading Torah and learning משנה are done in the סוכה, but analyzing the material is done outside the סוכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's line 'he learns in the סוכה' by quoting רבא, who seems to say some learning should be done outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says to learn in the סוכה with no limits. רבא splits learning into two kinds and sends the deeper kind (תנויי, working through the reasons) outside the סוכה. So they seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The covered booth, i.e., the סוכה
Analyzing, delving into the reasons of the משנה

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rava say:
Reading Scripture and learning Mishnah — in the sukkah,
but analyzing — outside the sukkah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last detail of the ברייתא in Step 24, 'ומשנן בסוכה'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that one learns Torah in the סוכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא says in-depth analysis is done outside the סוכה, which contradicts an unlimited rule of learning inside it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying learning is forbidden in the סוכה. He agrees that basic learning happens there. Only the deep analysis is placed outside.

steps.title: Review inside, deep analysis outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves: the ברייתא means review and memorizing; רבא means in-depth analysis.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (the ברייתא) speaks of reviewing the text; that (רבא) speaks of in-depth analysis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources are talking about two different kinds of learning, so there is no contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going over material (גירסא) is a normal home activity and belongs in the סוכה, as the ברייתא says. Deep analysis (עיון) needs a quiet, comfortable place to concentrate, so רבא places it outside the סוכה. Each source refers to a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... that one (each source refers to a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: The סוכה is your home for 7 days (תשבו כעין תדורו): nice dishes, bedding, eating, drinking, relaxing and Torah review all go there. Deep analysis may be done outside, because it needs a place where one can concentrate.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this (the baraita) refers to reviewing the text,
that (Rava) refers to in-depth analysis.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — בְּמִגְרַס, הָא — בְּעַיּוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בהא): each source speaks about a different type of learning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רבא both refer to all Torah learning and therefore contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to review (גירסא), which is done in the סוכה. רבא refers to deep analysis (עיון), which may be done outside.
